Guardian contract (machine-readable front matter — parsed by the Guardian pipeline) ```yaml guardian_issue: id: "SDK-C6" title: "Multi-language verifiers — Python + TypeScript envelope/chain/anchor verification" epic: "Strategy A — the signed trail is checkable anywhere (D-1 / D-2)" status: planned priority: medium created_at: "2026-09-25T00:00:00Z" dependencies: - name: "SDK-SCHEMAS-PUBLISH (#18)" type: internal note: "The non-Rust verifiers consume the published `rigorix-schemas` corpus (do not re-vendor)." - name: "rigorix-verifier (Rust, #19)" type: internal note: "Reference implementation + the byte-exact parity bar the others must meet." intent: | Strategy A (D-2) is "schemas + per-language envelope verifiers so the HMAC-signed trail is independently checkable in any CI / by any downstream consumer". Only the Rust verifier exists today, so the cross-language claim is half-delivered: a Python/TS user cannot verify a rigorix envelope without shelling out to Rust. Ship `python/` and `typescript/` verifiers that reproduce the SAME proofs byte-exact. in_scope: - "`python/` package (`rigorix-verifier`): verify an envelope HMAC (canonical form), JSON-Schema conformance, a per-producer chain (+ checkpoint-covered gaps), and the three Ed25519 anchor artifacts (receipt/history-slice/compaction-checkpoint)." - "`typescript/` package: the same surface for Node (crypto/HMAC + a JSON-Schema validator + an Ed25519 implementation, e.g. @noble/ed25519)." - "Both MUST reproduce the canonical bytes exactly (field order, `signature` nulled, sorted maps) — proven against the SAME committed fixtures (`schemas/fixtures/envelope/*`, `schemas/fixtures/integrity/*`) the Rust verifier uses." - "Consume the contract corpus from the published `rigorix-schemas` (or a pinned copy of it), not from a repo-relative path." - "A conformance test in each language asserting the committed fixtures verify byte-exact (mirrors the Rust `engine_signed_fixtures_verify_byte_exact` + `sdk_anchor_fixtures_match_enterprise_signing_bytes`)." - "Publishable (PyPI / npm) with READMEs + license; a CI job per language." out_of_scope: - "Typed API clients (SDK-C4 / #11) — verifiers only here." - "Java/Go verifiers (follow-ups once Python + TS are stable)." - "Any rigorix-engine/execution logic (D-1: protocol-only)." affected_layers: python: - "create: python/ (package, tests, README, pyproject.toml)" typescript: - "create: typescript/ (package, tests, README, package.json)" ci: - "modify: .github/workflows/ci.yml (per-language jobs)" canonical_references: - doc: "rigorix-sdk docs/strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md (D-1, D-2)" - code: "rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs (canonical byte form, verify_signature, verify_chain, verify_chain_with_checkpoints, verify_ed25519)" - fixtures: "schemas/fixtures/envelope/*, schemas/fixtures/integrity/* (the parity corpus)" acceptance_criteria: - "[ ] Python verifier: HMAC + schema + chain + Ed25519, green against the committed fixtures byte-exact" - "[ ] TypeScript verifier: same surface, same fixtures, byte-exact" - "[ ] Both reject tampered envelopes, broken chains, and bad anchor signatures (negative tests)" - "[ ] Both consume the contract corpus without a repo-relative path (packaged)" - "[ ] CI green per language; packages publishable" validators: [ci, tests, architecture, canonical] implementation_notes: | - Independent re-implementation is the POINT (Strategy A): do not shell out to the Rust verifier. Cross-check against it via the shared fixtures instead. - Canonical form is the hard part: `serde_json::to_string(envelope with signature=None)` with the engine's struct field ORDER and sorted map keys. Reproduce byte-exact or the HMAC fails. Document the field order in each README. - Anchor artifacts sign with Ed25519 over compact JSON of the artifact with `sig=null` (see `schemas/fixtures/integrity/README.md`); the receipt/slice/checkpoint fixtures verify under the documented public key `ea4a6c63…d22c` (seed [7u8;32]). - Prefer generating the frozen envelope/struct field order from `rigorix-schemas` (or a small codegen) so all languages share one order; a hand-copied order will drift. file_changes: - "create: python/**" - "create: typescript/**" - "modify: .github/workflows/ci.yml" pipeline_steps: [implement, validate, create-mr, merge] ```
# SDK-C6: multi-language verifiers (Python + TypeScript) ## Problem The freeze's Strategy A is "schemas + per-language envelope verifiers … checkable in any CI / by any downstream consumer" (D-2). Only the **Rust** verifier exists, so a Python or Node consumer cannot verify a rigorix envelope without shelling out to Rust — the "anywhere" claim is half-delivered. ## Approach Ship `python/` and `typescript/` verifiers that reproduce the **same** proofs byte-exact, proven against the **same** committed fixtures the Rust verifier uses: - envelope HMAC (canonical form), JSON-Schema conformance - per-producer chain (incl. checkpoint-covered gaps) - the three Ed25519 anchor artifacts (receipt / history-slice / compaction-checkpoint) Both consume the contract corpus from the published `rigorix-schemas` (SDK-SCHEMAS-PUBLISH), not a repo-relative path. ## Why this matters The enterprise already runs the HMAC check in Rust; the demos/CI run it in Rust. A language-neutral verifier is what makes an external auditor able to check the trail with their own stack — the trust multiplier the freeze names. ## Canonical references - `docs/strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md` (D-1, D-2) - Rust reference: `rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs` - Parity corpus: `schemas/fixtures/{envelope,integrity}/*` ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Python verifier byte-exact on the committed fixtures | pytest | | 2 | TypeScript verifier byte-exact on the committed fixtures | vitest/jest | | 3 | Negative tests (tamper, broken chain, bad sig) | per language | | 4 | No repo-relative corpus dependency | package | | 5 | CI green per language | CI |
title: SDK-C6: multi-language verifiers — Python + TypeScript (Strategy A parity)

# SDK-CATALOG-AUDIT: declare the three Phase B audit methods ## Problem The enterprise ADR-016 Phase B ledger (rigorix-enterprise #207 / PR #210, merged) registers three methods in its `CatalogRouter` that the frozen catalog does not declare: ``` rigorix.audit.head MethodKind::Query, AuthLevel::Session, mcp_tool: None rigorix.audit.history MethodKind::Query, AuthLevel::Session, mcp_tool: None rigorix.audit.overdue MethodKind::Query, AuthLevel::Session, mcp_tool: None ``` `schema/api/catalog.json` has only `rigorix.audit.read` / `.list` / `.summary`. Under **D-3** ("a server implements a subset and MUST NOT extend the namespace") this is drift — the exact class SDK-C5 fixed for `rigorix.auth.verify`, and what `verify_catalog_subset` guards. ## Evidence ``` $ # enterprise catalog (13 methods) minus SDK catalog (20 methods): undeclared = ['rigorix.audit.head', 'rigorix.audit.history', 'rigorix.audit.overdue'] $ grep -rn "audit.head|audit.history|audit.overdue" rigorix-sdk/schemas (no hits) ``` Nothing catches it: the enterprise has no `verify_catalog_subset` call (ENT-CATALOG-SUBSET-GUARD). ## Shapes (enterprise = code truth) | Method | params | result | |---|---|---| | `rigorix.audit.head` | `{ producer_id: string }` | ledger head `{ producer_id, sequence, envelope_hash }` (nullable) | | `rigorix.audit.history` | `{ producer_id: string, since?: date-time }` | the frozen **`api/history-slice.json`** shape (reuse) | | `rigorix.audit.overdue` | `{ threshold_secs?: integer }` | `{ threshold_secs, count, runs: [{ execution_id, status, registered_at }] }` | ## Canonical references - ADR-0001 (D3) · ADR-016 (Phase B) - enterprise `catalog.rs` / `services.rs` / `dto.rs`; SDK `api/history-slice.json` ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Three methods declared with `$defs` | review + catalog_integrity | | 2 | `history` result reuses `history-slice` | review | | 3 | Enterprise 13-method set passes `verify_catalog_subset` | CI (ENT guard) | | 4 | Docs + delta note | review | | 5 | CI green | CI |

# SDK-VERIFIER-PUBLISH: publish `rigorix-verifier` ## Problem `rigorix-verifier` is verified and useful, but not distributable: it reads the contracts from a directory outside its crate root, so `cargo package` ships zero schemas and the published crate's schema/catalog/chain functions cannot run. Reusing it requires publishing it self-contained. ## Evidence ``` $ cargo package -p rigorix-verifier --list .cargo_vcs_info.json Cargo.lock Cargo.toml Cargo.toml.orig src/lib.rs # ← no schemas, no README, no LICENSE $ cargo package ... | grep -c schemas 0 ``` ## Approach 1. Depend on `rigorix-schemas` (SDK-SCHEMAS-PUBLISH) and resolve contracts from it, keeping `RIGORIX_SDK_SCHEMAS` as an override. 2. Complete the publish metadata (README/license/keywords/categories/MSRV). 3. Add a CI job that **packages → unpacks → builds → smoke-tests** the crate with no env var — the only proof that matters for a published crate. 4. Publish + tag. ## Payoff (cross-repo) - **rigorix-oss** `server/tests/catalog_parity.rs` drops its inline subset re-check for `rigorix-verifier::verify_catalog_subset` (OSS-CATALOG-SUBSET-VERIFIER). - **rigorix-enterprise** adds it as a dev-dependency to wire the subset guard (ENT-CATALOG-SUBSET-GUARD), which would have caught the currently-undeclared `rigorix.audit.head` / `.history` / `.overdue`. ## Canonical references - ADR-0001 · `docs/strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md` (D-1, D-2) - `rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs` (`schema_path`, `verify_catalog_subset`, `verify_chain`, `verify_signature`) ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Resolution: env override -> embedded schemas (no `../../schemas`) | unit | | 2 | `cargo test` green in the packaged crate with the env unset | CI (packaged) | | 3 | package -> unpack -> build -> smoke test green, no env | CI | | 4 | `cargo publish --dry-run` green + full metadata | CI | | 5 | Published + tagged | release |

Today they exist only in the repo, and `rigorix-verifier` reads them from a path OUTSIDE its crate root (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../schemas`) — so `cargo package` ships ZERO schemas and a published verifier's schema/catalog functions (`verify_signature`, `verify_catalog_subset`, `all_schemas_compile`, `catalog_integrity`, `verify_chain`) cannot run. add a `cargo package` step)" canonical_references: - adr: "rigorix-sdk docs/adr/ADR-0001-native-api-catalog.md" - doc: "rigorix-sdk docs/strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md (D-1: schemas = single source of truth; D-2: schemas + verifiers)" - code: "rigorix-sdk schemas/** (corpus); rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs::schema_path (today's out-of-crate read at `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../schemas`)" acceptance_criteria: - "[ ] `rigorix-schemas` embeds every file under `schemas/**` (schemas AND `fixtures/**`) and returns them by relative path" - "[ ] A sync test fails when the embedded corpus diverges from the on-disk `schemas/**`" - "[ ] `cargo package -p rigorix-schemas` succeeds; the packaged crate builds standalone with no path/env dependency on the repo" - "[ ] The `$id` -> file map is exposed for cross-file `$ref` registration" - "[ ] CI green (fmt · clippy · test · package)" validators: [ci, tests, architecture, canonical] implementation_notes: | - Prefer build-time embedding so the published crate has NO runtime file dependency. A `build.rs` that walks `schemas/` and writes a `&[(&str, &str)]` table into `OUT_DIR` keeps the source of truth on disk and makes the sync test trivial. - Keep the crate near dependency-free (at most `serde_json`) — it is data + lookup, not logic. No `rigorix-engine` dependency (D-1). - crates.io name `rigorix-schemas` verified AVAILABLE (no sparse-index entry as of 2026-09-25). - The crate version should ride the same train as the schemas freeze; publish it before the verifier so the verifier can depend on a published version. file_changes: - "create: rust/rigorix-schemas/{Cargo.toml, build.rs, src/lib.rs, README.md}" - "modify: rust/Cargo.toml" - "modify: .github/workflows/ci.yml" pipeline_steps: [implement, validate, create-mr, merge] ```
# SDK-SCHEMAS-PUBLISH: publish the canonical contracts as a crate ## Problem The contracts in `schemas/` are the SDK's primary artifact, but they are not distributable. `rigorix-verifier` resolves them at runtime from `RIGORIX_SDK_SCHEMAS` or `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../schemas` — a directory **outside the crate root**, so it is never part of the package. ## Evidence ``` $ cargo package -p rigorix-verifier --list .cargo_vcs_info.json Cargo.lock Cargo.toml Cargo.toml.orig src/lib.rs # ← 0 schemas $ cargo package ... | grep -c schemas 0 ``` A consumer of the published verifier therefore cannot validate a signature, a catalog subset, a chain, or any schema — every schema-dependent entry point errors with *"schema not found … set RIGORIX_SDK_SCHEMAS"*. ## Approach (option B — chosen) Publish a companion **`rigorix-schemas`** crate that embeds `schemas/**` and exposes it by name. Keep the root `schemas/` canonical; generate the embedded table at build time and guard it with a sync test. This makes the contract consumable by the Rust verifier, the future Python/TS verifiers, and both servers — one copy, one version. ## Why not vendoring into the verifier (option A) Option A (a `schemas/` copy inside `rigorix-verifier/`) publishes the verifier alone, but the non-Rust verifiers (SDK-C6) and the servers would each re-vendor — exactly the drift the freeze wants to avoid. Option B makes the **contract** the published unit (D-1: "schemas = single source of truth"). ## Canonical references - ADR-0001 (catalog contract) · `docs/strategy-freeze-2026-09-06.md` (D-1, D-2) - `rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs::schema_path` (the current out-of-crate read) ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Every `schemas/**` file (incl. fixtures) is embedded and retrievable | unit | | 2 | Sync test fails on embedded-vs-disk divergence | unit | | 3 | `cargo package` succeeds; packaged crate builds standalone | CI | | 4 | `$id` map exposed | unit | | 5 | CI green | CI |

# SDK-C4: Typed SDK clients against the frozen catalog (Rust + TypeScript) ## Intent Ship the first typed clients over the frozen `rigorix.*` catalog. Thin, protocol-only (no engine dep), governed-flows-only. Rust is the reference (mirrors `rigorix-verifier`); TypeScript proves the catalog is language-neutral. ## Dependencies ``` ADR-0001 (catalog freeze, done) │ ├──────────────► C4 typed clients (THIS ISSUE, rigorix-sdk) │ │ e2e needs │ ▼ └──────────────► C2 rigorix-server (rigorix-oss) ``` ## In Scope - `rust/rigorix-client` — typed methods, JSON-RPC transport, error mapping, device-flow auth helpers, version negotiation. - `typescript/` — same surface, idiomatic TS. - Catalog-drift test (every method bound or explicitly server-only). - Live e2e against C2 (Rust): plan → run → audit.read. - Per-client README (transport, auth, D5 invariant). ## Out of Scope - Python / Java / Go (follow-ups). - The verifier (exists). Server changes (C2/C3). - Embedded execution (D-6). Publishing/release automation. ## Affected Layers ### Clients - New: `rust/rigorix-client/` (lib, types, transport, error, auth) - New: `typescript/` (index, types, transport, error) ### Tests - New: `catalog_binding.rs` (drift), `e2e_server.rs` (gated on C2) - New: TS transport/error tests ### Docs - New: `rust/rigorix-client/README.md`, `typescript/README.md` ## Canonical References - **ADR-0001** — D2/D4/D5/D6/D9/D10 - **catalog** `schemas/api/catalog.json` (types) · **errors** `schemas/api/errors.json` - **precedent** `rust/rigorix-verifier` (protocol-only, no engine dep) - **backlog** `rigorix-oss docs/next-workstreams-2026-09-21.md` §C4 ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Rust client has NO `rigorix-engine` dep | `cargo tree` in CI | | 2 | TS client builds + tests pass | CI | | 3 | Drift test fails on an unbound catalog method | unit test | | 4 | Error taxonomy maps every `data.type`; unknown → generic (no panic) | unit test | | 5 | Batch + notification framing tested | unit test | | 6 | `rigorix.system.version` negotiation exposed | unit test | | 7 | Live e2e plan → run → audit.read validates | e2e (C2) | | 8 | No raw step-execution surface | review + drift test | | 9 | CI green | CI | ## Implementation Notes - **Reuse, don't invent.** Type fields mirror `catalog.json` `$defs` exactly. A missing shape is a catalog change, not a client-local type. - Transport stays dumb: framing + auth header + error decode. No policy logic. - D5: display-only identity fields must not be presented as authorization. - Model `rigorix-client` on `rust/rigorix-verifier` (protocol-only, no engine dep). - Gate the e2e test behind a server-URL env var so the crate is usable before C2. ## DoD - [ ] Rust + TS clients build/test green; no-engine-dep assertion in CI - [ ] Drift test green; all 19 methods bound or exempted - [ ] e2e against C2 green (once C2 merges) - [ ] READMEs written
